identity.title: Extended Hα over compact far-infrared continuum in dusty submillimeter galaxies. Insights into dust distributions and star-formation rates at z ∼ 2

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using data from ALMA and near-infrared IFUs, we study the two-dimensional distributions of FIR continuum and H$\alpha$ for a sample of six $z\sim2$ SMGs.

question.value: Do the FIR (870 um) continuum and H-alpha have different sizes in z~2 SMGs, and what does this imply for dust attenuation, SFR estimates and SED modeling?

evidence.quote: In this paper we aim to extend the comparison between the FIR continuum and H$\alpha$ to a larger sample of SMGs.
an extra sample obtained through the program 2016.1.00735.S (PI: C. M. Harrison)

ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00307.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.01528.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00434, and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00735.S.
All ALMA data were tuned to the default band 7 continuum observations centered at 344 GHz/870 $\mu$m
covering the \[N ii\]/H$\alpha$ lines in all four sources

method.value: esorex/SPARK reduction; line fitting with AICc model selection per spectrum; adaptive binning up to 5x5 pixels

key_parameters.value: Delta chi2 > 16 for H-alpha-only, >9 per extra line

analysis_steps.goal: Measure sizes of H-alpha and 870 um via curve of growth

method.value: Circular-aperture curve of growth; half of normalised flux via spline linear fit; PSF subtracted in quadrature

evidence.quote: We use a spline linear fit to the measurements and derive the radius, along with the uncertainties, that corresponds to half of the normalized flux density.

validation.value: Compared with galfit Sersic major-axis sizes

evidence.quote: they are consistent with those obtained from the curve-of-growth methods

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Sersic profiles to H-alpha maps

evidence.quote: We limit the Sérsic index range to between 0.1 and 4

analysis_steps.goal: Measure 870 um flux and size in uv-plane

method.value: Elliptical Gaussian fits in visibilities; uvmultifit for ALESS75.1

evidence.quote: We measure their 870 $\mu$m continuum flux densities and sizes in the visibility domain using the casa package uvmodelfit assuming elliptical Gaussian profiles

validation.value: imfit flux ratio to uv flux 1.1+-0.1, no missing flux

evidence.quote: mean ratio of 1.1$\pm$0.1

analysis_steps.goal: Compare H-alpha SFRs with IR SFRs

method.value: hyperz UV-to-NIR fit for A_V; FIR template fitting for L_IR (8-1000 um); Kennicutt & Evans calibrations; attenuation relations from Calzetti and Kashino

evidence.quote: we estimate the star-formation rates based on H$\alpha$ and infrared luminosities by adopting the calibration provided by (cite: Kennicutt:2012aa)

key_parameters.value: A_V 0-5 in steps of 0.01; Calzetti law; BC03 templates

evidence.quote: We follow the (cite: Calzetti:2000aa) law to allow total attenuation ($A_V$) between 0 to 5 in steps of 0.01.

assumptions.value: Solar metallicity; four SFHs (B, E, Sb, C)

evidence.quote: assuming solar metallicities, with different SFHs

fitting.value: chi2 minimisation; A_V values from fits within Delta chi2<1

evidence.quote: take all the $A_V$ values from fits that have $\Delta\chi^2<1$ from the lowest $\chi^2$

validation.value: Reproduced Simpson et al. 2014 hyperz results

evidence.quote: We confirm that we are able to reproduce their results.

method.value: Differentiate H-alpha curve of growth; IR SFR profile follows 870 um profile scaled to total SFR; PSF deconvolved in quadrature

evidence.quote: the IR-based SFRs in each radial bin is the fraction of the total 870 $\mu$m flux in that bin multiplied by the total SFRs

assumptions.value: Constant dust temperature and opacity; same attenuation across radial bins

evidence.quote: This method effectively assumes a constant dust temperature and dust opacity

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of H-alpha SFR outside dusty region

evidence.quote: ranges from zero (AS2UDS412.0) to 40% (ALESS67.1)

findings_qualitative.value: FIR continuum is more compact than H-alpha and optical continuum; proposes a three-component dust model with a central heavily obscured component

evidence.quote: the heavily obscured central regions with low filling factor in which the bulk of attenuation cannot be reflected through H$\alpha$ or OIR continuum.

claims.hypothesis: H-alpha is more extended than FIR continuum in SMGs
claims.experiment: Curve-of-growth sizes of H-alpha and 870 um in six SMGs
claims.result: Median size ratio 2.0+-0.4; half differ by >3 sigma
claims.finding: H-alpha is larger than FIR continuum

evidence.quote: Across the sample the H$\alpha$ sizes are a median factor of ${2.0\pm0.4}$ larger than the FIR sizes.

claims.hypothesis: Attenuation-corrected H-alpha SFRs match IR SFRs
claims.experiment: Compare hyperz-corrected H-alpha SFRs with template-based IR SFRs
claims.result: Still lower by factor 3+-1 even with extreme correction
claims.finding: Bulk of obscured star formation is not traced by H-alpha

evidence.quote: the difference is still a factor of $3\pm1$

claims.hypothesis: Size mismatch explains the SFR discrepancy
claims.result: At most 40% of H-alpha SFR lies outside the dusty region
claims.finding: Size difference is not dominant; central heavy attenuation is

evidence.quote: the size difference in the global scale between the FIR continuum and H$\alpha$ is not the dominant factor

claims.hypothesis: Energy-balance SED fits give higher A_V than OIR-only fits
claims.result: magphys A_V higher in the highest L_IR sources

evidence.quote: We find that the A$_V$ values from magphys are significantly higher in two SMGs
